current_evidence: No newer list found: Halton's 'Apply for Planning' page (halton.gov.uk/planning-housing-your-environment/apply-planning) publishes no local list and only tells applicants to follow the validation checklist in each Planning Portal form. planning.data.gov.uk entity 20296 records this same committee appendix (ID 6473) as Halton's local area requirements. The document text gives no date.

issues.detail: The only Halton local list is an undated committee appendix ('Halton Borough Council Validation Checklists Requirements - Advice for officers and applicants') from about 2007-08. It cites revoked guidance (PPG24 1994, PPG13 2001, EIA Regs 1999, Circular 06/2005), the Halton UDP and pre-2020 use classes A3/A4/A5/B1. The council website does not publish it as a current local list, so it has almost certainly not been reviewed within the 2-year period and may carry little weight. The workbook should flag it as superseded or unmaintained, not simply 'Captured'.
issues.evidence: 3.7: 'Use Class A3 ... A4 ... A5, B1 and B2'; references to 'Planning Policy Guidance 24: Planning and Noise (September 1994)'; apply-planning page: 'You must use the help text and validation checklist for each form'

issues.detail: List date 2008-08-01 comes from the PDF CreationDate of an mgConvert2PDF on-the-fly conversion, not from the document text. The document text contains no adoption or publication date.
issues.evidence: Date basis 'PDF metadata CreationDate'; document text has no version or date

issues.detail: Grokbot's link is a councillors.halton.gov.uk mgConvert2PDF converter URL that robots.txt blocks. The same document has a stable URL at moderngov.halton.gov.uk/documents/s6473/Appendix a.pdf. tab_items is empty even though Extraction level says 'Full (automated)' and Req. items says 19.

Not captured: 3.12 Noise Assessment (developments raising noise disturbance to nearby occupants, or noise-sensitive development near existing noise sources) and 3.25 Travel Plan (applications likely to have significant transport implications). 3.3 Biodiversity Survey and Report is captured only as a generic 'Ecological Survey' row with a fragment trigger.
issues.evidence: 3.12: 'Applications for developments that raise issues of disturbance by noise to the occupants of nearby existing buildings...'; 3.25: 'A travel plan should be submitted alongside planning applications which are likely to have significant transport implications'

issues.detail: Sections 3.13-3.20 are absent from the readable text, which jumps from 3.12 to 3.21 and ends mid-sentence in 3.26. Grokbot also captured nothing from them, so eight local requirements (likely contamination, open space, parking, planning obligations, etc.) are unverified and missing from the workbook.
issues.evidence: Extracted text runs 3.1-3.12 then 3.21-3.26; ends 'Full guidance on the survey information,'

issues.detail: 'CIL Additional Information / Form' is not in the source. Its trigger text is the section 3.0 heading and introduction ('3.0 LOCAL REQUIREMENTS In addition to the information above ...'), plus the start of 3.1/3.2. The list predates the CIL Regulations 2010.
issues.evidence: 3.0 intro: 'Halton Borough Council will be require the following information to accompany certain applications'

issues.detail: Several triggers are garbled or cut off. Daylight/Sunlight: the excerpt is EIA and Flood Risk text, not the real trigger ('potential adverse impact upon the current levels of daylight/sunlight enjoyed by adjoining properties'). Transport Assessment: 'conversions. 3.24Transport Assessment mitigate transport impacts.' omits the trigger 'significant transport implications'. Environmental Statement: the excerpt is biodiversity text. Ecological, Heritage and Drainage/SuDS are mid-sentence fragments with no trigger. Street scene runs into Structural Survey and TA. Flood Risk contains the page-break debris '(Environmental 8'. Air Quality omits 'inside, or adjacent to an air quality management area'.
issues.evidence: 3.4: 'potential adverse impact upon the current levels of daylight/sunlight enjoyed by adjoining properties'; 3.1: 'inside, or adjacent to an air quality management area'

issues.detail: Four requirements are placed under Listed building consent only because the phrase 'listed building' appears nearby. Lighting Assessment applies to publicly accessible development near residential property, a listed building, a conservation area or open countryside, not to LBC applications. Landscaping Details and the Design and Access Statement row (whose trigger is the landscaping/lighting text) are not LBC-specific. The source's Structural Survey trigger is substantial demolition, e.g. barn conversions. Meanwhile the 13 Full planning rows are all 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', and Householder, Outline, Demolition in conservation area etc. show '(none)', although several items (Heritage Statement for conservation area consent, Tree Survey, Flood Risk, Street Scene) apply to those types.
issues.evidence: 3.11: 'Proposals involving the provision of publicly accessible developments, in the vicinity of residential property, a listed building or conservation area, or open countryside'; 3.23: 'involves substantial demolition, e.g. barn conversions'

issues.detail: The Design and Access Statement row under Listed building consent is a national requirement (cross-referenced to section 2.6), not a local item, and its trigger text is about landscaping and lighting.
issues.evidence: 3.10: 'follow from the design concept in the Design and Access Statement (see Section 2.6 Design & Access Statement)'

summary: Grokbot's link is a robots-blocked converter URL for Halton's only identifiable local list, an undated c.2007-08 committee appendix that the council no longer publishes and that should be flagged as stale. Grokbot's extraction invents a CIL requirement, misses Noise Assessment and Travel Plan, has many garbled triggers, and misplaces items under Listed building consent.
